subject: ACME: Performance SLOs & concurrency follow-up / rate limits
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@acme.com>, ACME Platform Team <platform@acme.com>
Cc: 
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: ACME: Performance SLOs & concurrency follow-up / rate limits
Attachments: acme-slo-table.xlsx

Hi Ellen / ACME Platform Team,

Thanks again for taking the call this morning - good conversation. Quick recap + a few follow-ups so we can align on a perf pilot and the initial quota request.

Call recap (high level):
- ACME target product SLOs: 150ms p50 and <= 600ms p95 for typical single-request generation (non-streaming).
- Streaming requirements: some chat flows use server-sent events (SSE) / chunked streaming; p95 end-to-end for first token should be <= 1s and steady-state token latency < 40ms.
- Expected steady throughput: ~200 RPS during business hours; peak bursts up to ~600 RPS for short promo windows.
- Concurrency: roughly 120 concurrent in-flight requests at peak (chat-heavy). You also mentioned connection pooling from the frontend -> backend with long-lived keep-alive connections.

Questions / asks for the pilot:
1) Can you confirm whether the 120 concurrent number is concurrent in-flight requests or concurrent websocket/SSE connections? (they have different implications for quotas).
2) Can you share a simple traffic shape (RPS over time) or the spreadsheet I requested so we can model batching, KV cache hit-rates, and token budget? I attached our sample SLO table - if you fill the traffic column it helps us size a reserved pool.
3) Any hard limits on allowed request/connection timeouts from your side (e.g. 60s max for one request)?

Initial Redwood proposal (ballpark; exact numbers to follow after we get your traffic shape):
- Reserved concurrency: 120 in-flight requests with a burst buffer to 180 for short spikes.
- Connection limit: 600 concurrent HTTP/1.1 keep-alive connections (to support pooling/SDK keep-alive).
- Request rate limit: 500 RPS sustained, 900 RPS burst for 2 minutes.
- Token rate limit: 60k tokens/minute (can be increased for Dedicated).
- Streaming: supported; streaming connections count against connection limit but not all streaming traffic will consume in-flight slots unless actively generating.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm the concurrency vs connections distinction and attach the traffic shape (reply to this thread).
- We provision a pilot pool based on the numbers above and run a 48h perf run (we'll provide a JMeter-like load script and a sample prompt set).
- If perf looks good, we lock in quotas and send the updated rate-limits proposal and contract addendum.

Thanks - happy to jump on a 30m follow-up if that helps.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@acme.com>

Date: Mon, 27 Jul 2026 10:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME: Performance SLOs & concurrency follow-up / rate limits

Thanks Marissa - quick answers and context below.

1) Concurrency vs connections:
- The 120 number is concurrent in-flight requests (we mean active API calls that are waiting on tokens/response).
- We typically maintain ~400 long-lived frontend -> backend keep-alive connections for pooling, but only a subset are active at any moment.

2) Traffic shape: attaching a weekly traffic export (see acme-slo-table.xlsx). Peak pattern: 200 RPS steady, with marketing bursts to ~650 RPS for 5-10 minute windows (2-3 times per day during promos).

3) Timeouts: the frontend enforces a 90s timeout for generation requests; anything beyond we treat as failed. For streaming sessions we close idle streams after 5 minutes.

Other notes:
- We do some batching on the backend (typically small batches of 2-4 requests) but want to avoid excessive batching for latency-sensitive flows.
- Tokens per generation vary: normal chat messages ~150 tokens, long-form generation up to 1,200 tokens (less common).

Action: please send a concrete pilot config & a proposed initial quota. Also include any SDK/connection tuning recommendations for our frontend (keep-alive, pool size, socket timeout).

—Ellen
Ellen Park
Senior Engineer, Platform
ACME Corp
ellen.park@acme.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, ACME Platform Team <platform@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME: Performance SLOs & concurrency follow-up / rate limits

Hi Ellen - thanks for the details and the spreadsheet. Based on the traffic shape and your timeouts, here's a concrete pilot configuration we can stand up for 48h testing: 

Pilot config (48h):
- Reserved in-flight concurrency: 150 (this covers your 120 peak plus headroom).
- Burst in-flight concurrency: allow up to 220 for short windows (auto-throttle after 3 minutes).
- Connection limit: 600 long-lived keep-alive connections (matches your pool).
- Request rate limit: 750 RPS sustained, 950 RPS burst for up to 3 minutes.
- Token rate limit: 100,000 tokens/minute for the pilot.
- Streaming config: streaming connections will be permitted up to the connection limit; for steady-state streaming we expect per-token latency ~30-50ms on our GPU-backed hosting.

Notes/assumptions:
- We assume average tokens per request ~200 for pilot modeling; please flag if your average differs significantly.
- Batching: we will keep batching conservative for this pilot (max batch size 4) to meet the p95 latency target.
- Failure model: if tail latency or error rate exceeds our internal gates during pilot, traffic will be routed to a lower-cost fallback model; we'll notify you via the console and Slack integration.

Next steps:
1) Marissa to provision the pilot pool and share credentials + a short runbook for your infra team (sample load script + expected metrics).
2) ACME to run a single test day (you can start with a 2-hr ramp) and we collect perf & token billing metrics.
3) We review results and finalize quotas. If the pilot meets SLOs, we will convert the pilot config into a committed Dedicated/reserved capacity quote and addendum.

I've attached a preliminary PDF proposal with the rate limits and the above config. Marissa - can you provision the pool and send the runbook today?

Best,
Laura Bennett
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
